chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text: Volyx Lens is a compact glass overlay that can use three intentionally separate inputs:

chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text:
- **Screen** — screenshots are captured only for an explicit screen-based action.
- **Microphone / “You”** — your voice is transcribed on its own channel.
- **System audio / “Them”** — a native ScreenCaptureKit helper captures meeting audio on a separate channel.

chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text: Nothing is routed through a VolyxAI server. Provider requests go directly from the app to the AI or transcription provider you configure.

chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text:
- **Screen-aware assistance** — ask about the visible screen, a conversation, or both.
- **Separated meeting transcript** — stable timestamped **You** and **Them** turns.
- **Task Context** — save multiple screens locally, pin important captures, deduplicate near-identical views, and attach a bounded relevant set only when you explicitly ask.
- **Provider choice** — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure Foundry, and DeepSeek for responses; OpenAI, Azure, Deepgram, or optional local Whisper for transcription.
- **Personal context** — import a resume/CV and job description with bounded extraction and relevance selection.
- **Local controls** — clear sessions, export transcripts, inspect sanitized diagnostics, and stop capture immediately.
- **Native macOS behavior** — compact draggable overlay, edge-aware expanded docking, Keychain-backed credential storage, and best-effort capture exclusion.

chunks.text: Volyx Lens is an Electron application with a sandboxed renderer and a privileged main process:

chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text:
1. **Capture stays separated.** Screens, microphone PCM, and system-audio PCM have distinct lifecycles.
2. **Local controls run first.** Permission checks, memory budgets, deduplication, OCR ranking, cancellation, and secure credential access happen locally.
3. **The user triggers a request.** Screen and transcript context is attached only for the selected action.
4. **The main process routes directly.** Requests go to the configured response or transcription provider—never through a VolyxAI intermediary.
5. **Results stream into the overlay.** Provider failures are reduced to sanitized, actionable states rather than exposing credentials or raw SDK errors.

chunks.title: Volyx Lens
chunks.text: Realtime microphone audio is deterministically resampled to 24 kHz mono PCM. System audio comes from a bundled ScreenCaptureKit helper and remains a separate **Them** channel. Optional local Whisper is operator-configured, disabled by default, and does not silently fall back to cloud transcription unless cloud fallback is separately enabled.

chunks.title: Local Review Intelligence
chunks.text: By default, runtime review data, embeddings, and prompts are processed by embedded Chroma and Ollama on the same machine. If `OLLAMA_HOST` points to another computer or hosted endpoint, prompts and retrieved review excerpts are sent there. Installing dependencies and downloading models also use the network.

chunks.title: Local Review Intelligence

chunks.title: Local Review Intelligence
chunks.text: - **Visual dashboard:** adaptive metrics, distribution charts, rating/date/category filters, a review browser, and a grounded-question surface. - **Validated citations:** short evidence citations map strictly to stable retrieved source IDs; an invalid or premature-abstention response gets one bounded correction attempt, then invented or missing citations fail safely. - **Safe offline state:** analytics still load when Ollama is unavailable, while the app shows exact setup commands instead of crashing. - **Adaptive CSV upload:** automatically detect common headers, manually map unfamiliar names, and isolate every dataset in content-addressed Chroma storage. - **Reconciled indexing:** content-derived IDs survive reordering; additions, changed records, and deletions are synchronized safely. - **Measured RAG:** a versioned 30-case evaluation across nine answerable domains plus abstention

chunks.title: Local Review Intelligence
chunks.text: compares semantic retrieval with a deterministic BM25 keyword baseline, then measures citation validity, a transparent reference-term support proxy, expected-action accuracy, answer success, and abstention recall. - **Installable CLI:** the packaged `local-ai-agent` command exposes status, ask, chat, and evaluate workflows. - **Local execution by default:** Ollama handles embeddings and answer generation unless a remote host is explicitly configured.

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: A temporal machine-learning pipeline for football forecasting and evaluation. It produces calibrated Home/Draw/Away probabilities, combines an XGBoost classifier with independent-Poisson score estimates, and keeps frozen backtests, live forecasts and synthetic interface data separate.

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: **Status:** experimental research and engineering project. The forecasts are uncertain estimates, not betting advice or evidence of future profitability.

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: The repository includes an auditable rolling-origin evaluation built from six Premier League seasons. Its source URLs, file hashes, temporal windows and fold outputs are checked in as a narrative report and machine-readable JSON.

chunks.text:
| Measure | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Untouched chronological test matches | 1,140 |
| Model weighted accuracy | 53.77% |

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: The model beat its naive accuracy, log-loss and Brier baselines in all three folds, but it did not beat the bookmaker benchmark. Model accuracy covered all 1,140 test rows; the bookmaker’s selective accuracy covered 1,125 rows (98.68%) because 15 closing-probability ties were treated as abstentions. The report is checked-in, auditable evidence; the repository does not yet provide one command that regenerates that exact football-data.co.uk benchmark end to end. The operational backfill path described below uses Football-data.org and optional FBref collection, so it is a separate data workflow.

chunks.text: Backtesting is not live forecasting

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: Backtesting evaluates a model on historical matches after fitting and calibration on earlier windows. It does not prove how future live forecasts will perform. Separately generated `run_kind=backtest` rows remain isolated for provenance, and the frozen bundle report remains the authoritative holdout result.

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text: The dataset is ordered by kickoff time and split into disjoint training, calibration and test windows. Goal-model features for the classifier are generated out of fold with expanding chronological training windows. The fitted classifier is calibrated on the separate calibration window. Its probabilities are blended at a fixed 50/50 weight with Home/Draw/Away probabilities derived from fitted home and away goal rates under an independent-Poisson assumption. The untouched test window is evaluated once and stored in the versioned bundle.

chunks.title: Football Forecasting Lab
chunks.text:
- **Selective accuracy:** correct predictions among rows with one unique highest-probability outcome. Probability ties are abstentions; the report shows the evaluated denominator, abstention count and coverage.
- **Log loss:** penalizes confident wrong probabilities. Lower is better.
- **Multiclass Brier:** mean squared error across Home/Draw/Away probabilities on the unscaled 0–2 range. Lower is better.
- **Classwise and maximum ECE:** calibration summaries. They are unstable on small samples and depend on binning.
- **Majority baseline:** selects the most common training-window outcome and uses the same non-tied holdout subset as selective accuracy.
- **Prior-probability baseline:** assigns the training-window class frequencies to every holdout match.

- Provider availability, coverage and historical completeness vary.
- Calibration estimates are unstable on small holdouts.
- Historical results can become stale under distribution shift.
- Live accuracy alone does not measure probability quality, and the API does not expose log loss, Brier score, calibration error or evaluation dates.

- The scheduler is disabled unless `ENABLE_SCHEDULER=true`.

- Only allowlisted social domains are accepted.

chunks.title: Telegram Social Video Downloader
chunks.text: Read `SECURITY.md` and `docs/security.md` before exposing the service outside a private network.

chunks.title: Telegram Social Video Downloader
chunks.text:
- Designed for a **single downloader instance**. SQLite is durable, but it is not a distributed queue.
- Delivery is at-least-once: a crash after Telegram accepts media but before SQLite records success can cause one duplicate delivery after restart.
- yt-dlp follows extractor-selected redirects. Run the container on a network without access to cloud metadata or internal administration services.
- Platform changes can break yt-dlp extraction; keep yt-dlp current and test upgrades.

chunks.title: Solana and Ethereum Wallet Analyzer
chunks.text: The web application does not use cookies, analytics, local storage, session storage, accounts, or a wallet-connection library. It does not persist submitted addresses. CSV and JSON exports are generated locally in the browser. Share links place the address after `#`, which prevents it from being included in the HTTP request; the address remains visible in the URL and browser history, and opening the link only pre-fills the form until the user submits it. Its in-memory rate limiter stores only bounded client identifiers and request timestamps for the configured window. Submitted public addresses are still sent to the configured Solana RPC, the configured Ethereum JSON-RPC provider (PublicNode by default), CoinGecko, or DexScreener as required for analysis. Token logos are fetched by the server from DexScreener's allowlisted image CDN and served through a same-origin endpoint, so the

chunks.title: Solana and Ethereum Wallet Analyzer
chunks.text: browser does not contact the image provider; only validated raster formats up to 512 KiB are accepted, and missing or failed images fall back to a symbol monogram. Logo payloads use a separate byte-budgeted cache capped at 8 MiB and 256 entries per worker, with at most eight active upstream fetches and 32 admitted jobs, same-mint request coalescing, and short-lived negative caching. Excess distinct jobs fail closed to the monogram fallback. Operators should configure trusted proxy handling deliberately before relying on forwarded client IPs.

chunks.title: Solana and Ethereum Wallet Analyzer
chunks.text: The Telegram bot stores Telegram user IDs, names, usernames, language codes, join/last-active timestamps, and interaction counters in `user_data.json`. The file is written atomically with owner-only permissions on supported systems, but it is still plaintext. Operators are responsible for access control, backups, retention, deletion requests, and an appropriate privacy notice.

chunks.title: Solana and Ethereum Wallet Analyzer

- Ethereum RPC errors, malformed responses, and timeouts stop that wallet report; they never produce a synthetic `0 ETH` result.
- Solana RPC errors, malformed responses, timeouts, and incomplete legacy/Token-2022 account queries stop that wallet report with a retryable warning.
- Native-price requests use Coinbase first and CoinGecko as a fallback; reports stop only when both providers fail.
- Individual DexScreener metadata failures are omitted from token valuation and disclosed as partial data.
- HTTP 429 and server errors use bounded retries. Failed results are not cached as valid zero values.
- Refresh actions bypass the relevant five-minute caches.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text: A small async Telegram bot that registers unique users, reports counts to an admin, and sends durable milestone notifications.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text: The project favors verifiable behavior over benchmark claims: it has automated tests and CI, but it has **not** been load-tested for a specific throughput or user count.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text:
- Registers each Telegram user once with `/start`
- Returns the current unique-user count
- Sends admin notifications for every reached milestone
- Persists pending notifications so transient Telegram failures can be retried
- Restricts `/stats` to the configured admin
- Uses Redis for optional rate limiting and 60-second stats caching
- Supports SQLite for local use and PostgreSQL through Docker Compose
- Runs the application container as an unprivileged user on a read-only filesystem

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text:
1. A unique user and every newly reached milestone are committed in one database transaction.
2. Startup reconciles the current user count into any missing milestone rows before delivery.
3. Existing `admin_messages.last_count` state is used as the upgrade baseline, preventing historical milestones from being resent when the outbox table is introduced.
4. Pending notifications are sent in milestone order, stopping at the first failed send.
5. A successful notification is marked sent.
6. Stale pending rows at or below the delivered admin milestone are marked superseded instead of replacing newer state.
7. The previous admin message is deleted only after its replacement is delivered.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text: A Telegram send failure increments the attempt count and leaves the row pending. Pending rows are retried on application startup and after subsequent `/start` requests.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text: Redis is optional. If it is unavailable, the bot logs a warning and continues without distributed rate limiting or stats caching. Database-backed registration and milestones continue to work.

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text: The bot does **not** silently fall back to another database. Startup database failures stop initialization; handler-time failures are logged and return a generic user-facing error.

- Required and numeric configuration validation
- Gap-safe, idempotent milestone claims
- Atomic registration and milestone claims
- Startup reconciliation and legacy milestone baselines
- Ordered delivery that stops after the first failed milestone
- Failed notification retention and retry

- End-to-end registration and milestone delivery

chunks.title: User Count Telegram Bot
chunks.text:
- Run **one long-polling process per bot token**. Multiple `getUpdates` pollers for the same token are not a supported scaling strategy.
- The in-process notification lock prevents duplicate sends inside one process. The durable primary key prevents duplicate milestone claims in the database.
- Telegram delivery cannot be exactly-once: a process crash after Telegram accepts a message but before the database commit can cause a retry and duplicate message.
- There is no bot HTTP health endpoint, Prometheus integration, or published performance benchmark.
- For horizontal scaling, first move from long polling to a webhook architecture with centralized idempotency and distributed delivery locking, then benchmark the actual target workload.
